newsitem.title: USA: American States Q2 up ahead of merger.
newsitem.headline: American States Q2 up ahead of merger.

text.p: American States Financial Corp reported strong second quarter earnings and premium growth ahead of its previously agreed acquisition by Seattle-based SAFECO Funds.

"Importantly, we were able to post increases in net premium despite the distraction produced by our exploration of strategic options and the subsequent announcement of our agreement to be acquired by SAFECO," said Robert A. Anker, chairman and chief executive officer, in a statement.

The Indianapolis-based property-casualty insurer reported second-quarter operating earnings of $35.2 million or 59 cents per share, compared to $26.5 million in 1996, when, adjusted to reflect the effect of the company's initial public stock offering, operating earnings were 39 cents per share.
The second quarter brought year-to-date operating earnings to $81.4 million, up from $59.8 million in the first half of 1996.

Net written premium grew 2.9 percent, from $419.2 million in the second quarter of 1996 to $431.3 million in the current year. Exclusive of California and Florida, where the residual impact of action taken to reduce risk exposure persists, direct written premium increased 4.6 percent. For the year to date, net written premium was up 3.6 percent at $854.2 million, from $824.9 million a year earlier.
Anker said storm losses were near expectations and substantially below the unusually heavy levels of a year ago.
He said the premium growth indicated agent approval of the pending sale.

In a joint announcement June 9, ASFC and SAFECO announced an agreement for the Seattle-based insurer to acquire American States for $47.00 per share. That transaction is expected around the end of the third quarter, the company said.
